text:
Testing Methodology for Business Logic Vulnerabilities:
1. Workflow & State Mapping: Deconstruct target functionality into a formal state graph ($S_0 \to S_1 \to ... \to S_n$) identifying all implicit assumptions.
2. State Desynchronization / Skip Testing: Transmit terminal-step requests (e.g., checkout, confirmation) without executing prerequisite steps (e.g., payment submission, MFA validation).
3. Boundary & Non-Sensical Input Injection: Provide negative numeric quantities, zero-value balances, unexpected data types, or duplicate concurrent payloads to identify inadequate domain verification.
4. Client-Server Inconsistency Analysis: Intercept client-to-server payloads using a proxy to alter read-only or hidden parameters (e.g., price, discount_code, user_role, status_flag).

metadata.title: Logic Flaw Discovery and Workflow Auditing Methodology

text:
Testing methodology for unconventional input handling in business workflows:
1. Submit numeric extremes: negative values, zero, numbers exceeding integer limits (overflow/underflow), and high decimals.
2. Submit structural extremes: abnormally long strings, unicode characters, and null bytes into text fields.
3. Evaluate system responses against key boundary indicators: Does the application enforce hard constraints? Does it fail closed or open when limits are reached? Does it alter, truncate, or normalize the input unexpectedly?

metadata.title: Auditing and Fuzzing for Unconventional Input in Logic Controls

text:
Methodology for identifying excessive trust in transactional parameters:
1. Proxy passive observation: Map request parameters sent during state progression (e.g. POST /cart, POST /checkout) to check for monetary or role values.
2. In-flight parameter mutation: e.g. Intercept POST /cart, decrement numeric values to negative, zero, or small integers, and resubmit.
3. State diffing: Inspect subsequent cart retrieval (e.g. GET /cart) to verify whether the server persisted the injected value or reset it to the authoritative catalog value.

metadata.title: Transactional Parameter Tampering and Price Logic Auditing

text:
Testing methodology for unsigned numeric validation in e-commerce state machines:
1. Baseline Request Mapping: Identify all endpoints modifying order state or quantities (e.g., POST /cart, PUT /cart/items, POST /order/add).
2. Sign Inversion Injection: Intercept quantity parameters and submit negative integers (-1, -100, -999999).
3. Offset Calculation: Calculate the negative quantity required to cancel out high-value items present in the cart state without causing arithmetic underflow errors.
4. Differential State Analysis: Compare cart responses before and after negative submission to inspect line-item subtotals, overall cart balance, and checkout eligibility.

metadata.title: Numeric Sign Inversion Fuzzing on State Mutations

text: Methodology for auditing multi-channel identity update inconsistencies: 1) Identify endpoints assigning implicit trust or role elevation based on user profile fields (e.g., domain, department, organization code). 2) Map all entry points capable of mutating the trust-determining attribute (e.g., onboarding, profile settings, SSO sync, API PATCH endpoints). 3) Compare validation strictness across distinct mutation channels: check whether secondary profile update workflows bypass origin validation, format restrictions, or verification challenges enforced during initial registration. 4) Verify state persistence: confirm whether updated unverified attributes grant immediate access to protected routes.

metadata.title: Auditing Disparate Workflows for Inconsistent Security Controls

text: Methodology for auditing discount code and promotional application logic: 1) Identification: Harvest available promotional tokens, voucher strings, and gift card inputs. 2) Single-token boundary test: Replay the identical coupon token consecutively to assess immediate deduplication logic. 3) Multi-token permutation test: Interleave submissions of two or more distinct valid coupons (Token A -> Token B -> Token A) to determine if state tracking is naive/ephemeral. 4) Order lifecycle test: Verify whether applied discounts persist or reset if items are removed, modified, or re-added before final checkout submission.

metadata.title: Auditing Promotional Discount State Tracking and Replay Flaws

text: Auditing methodology for financial accumulation and primitive data type boundaries: 1) Input saturation test: Determine per-request validation limits on quantity and amount fields. 2) Boundary fuzzing via repetition: If single-payload input is bounded to small integers, automate high-volume sequential additions using single concurrency to evaluate aggregation logic. 3) Monitor state transitions for sign change: Inspect responses for sign flips indicative of 16-bit (32,767), 32-bit (2,147,483,647), or unsigned integer wrapping. 4) Wraparound alignment test: Calculate wrap offset ($Target = INT\_MAX + 1 - Wraparound$) to verify whether order placement logic evaluates wrapped negative or small values without sanity bounds.

metadata.title: Auditing Cumulative Fields for Primitive Integer Wraparound

text: Methodology for auditing multi-layer input length discrepancies and silent truncation: 1) Capacity probing: Submit unique identifiable strings of increasing lengths (e.g., 64, 128, 255, 256, 512, 1024 characters) into registration and profile fields. 2) Reflection diffing: Inspect the persisted profile view (GET /profile, API responses, or raw DB reflection) to detect silent truncation points. 3) Semantic boundary positioning: If truncation is identified at length N, craft composite strings where malicious or privileged suffixes align precisely at boundary index N, while operational routing elements (like controlled DNS subdomains) sit beyond index N. 4) Multi-channel verification: Confirm whether pre-persistence services (e.g., SMTP dispatch) operate on the untruncated string while post-persistence authorization components operate on the truncated string.

metadata.title: Auditing for Silent Truncation Discrepancies in Identity Workflows

text: Auditing methodology for dual-use endpoints and parameter-inferred privilege: 1) Identification: Catalog multi-parameter state-modifying requests (e.g., password change, profile updates, subscription adjustments). 2) Systematic parameter pruning: Iteratively drop each parameter individually (both key and value) while preserving other fields. 3) Branch behavior analysis: Observe whether missing parameters bypass checks, trigger default unauthenticated code branches, or bypass confirmation gates. 4) Identity substitution: When parameter omission bypasses validation, inject external/privileged identity handles into user-binding fields (e.g., username, uid, account_id) to verify if tenant/user isolation holds.

metadata.title: Systematic Parameter Omission and Identity Decoupling Auditing

text: Methodology for auditing multi-stage state machines and workflow validation: 1) Baseline transaction tracing: Execute a complete intended workflow ($S_0 \to S_1 \to ... \to S_n$) and record the URI, method, headers, and parameters for each transition step. 2) Transition skipping: Initialize a fresh workflow state, populate data elements, and directly transmit terminal step requests ($S_n$) without executing preceding processing requests ($S_{n-1}$, $S_{n-2}$). 3) Out-of-order execution: Test reordering steps (e.g., $S_0 \to S_2 \to S_1$) or replaying prior completion tokens in uninitialized sessions. 4) Verification: Inspect backend response status and state reflections to determine if processing advanced despite missing prerequisite states.

metadata.title: State Sequence Perturbation and Workflow Step-Skipping Auditing

text: Methodology for auditing multi-stage state machines via flow interruption: 1) Sequence tracing: Trace sequential interactions during multi-phase authentication, onboarding, or approval workflows. 2) Intermediary request dropping: Selectively drop each intermediate request (e.g., dropping step 2 of a 4-step sequence) using proxy interception rather than allowing it to reach the client or backend. 3) Out-of-order target navigation: Following the drop, initiate direct requests to subsequent steps ($S_3, S_4$) and root application views to inspect the state machine's fallback behavior. 4) State invariant auditing: Determine if the uncompleted flow defaults insecurely to elevated permissions, bypasses initialization routines, or leaks access to unfinalized profiles.

metadata.title: Auditing Multi-Stage Workflows via Flow Interruption and Request Dropping

text: Methodology for auditing circular economic loops and cash-equivalent arbitrage: 1) Asset classification: Identify all catalog items functioning as stored value, vouchers, loyalty tokens, or redeemable credit. 2) Discount eligibility probing: Apply percentage and fixed-value promotional codes to cart sessions containing cash-equivalent items to check if discounts apply. 3) Transaction cycle testing: Execute a complete purchase-to-redemption loop to compute net balance change ($\Delta = Value_{redeemed} - Cost_{settled}$). 4) Automation feasibility test: If $\Delta > 0$, construct a session handling macro or headless script chaining the sequential endpoints to evaluate whether stateful rate limits, deduplication controls, or velocity limits restrict continuous replay.

metadata.title: Auditing for Closed-Loop Currency Arbitrage and Discount Stacking

text: Methodology for auditing shared cryptographic contexts and oracle vulnerabilities: 1) State artifact cataloging: Collect all encrypted strings (cookies, hidden form tokens, query parameters, password reset blobs) across application states. 2) Oracle mapping: Identify reflection vectors where user-supplied inputs are encrypted into headers/cookies (encryption oracle), or where cookies/tokens are decrypted and reflected in UI errors/views (decryption oracle). 3) Context cross-pollination: Swap encrypted blobs between different parameters to assess if keys and algorithms are shared across functions. 4) Block cipher characterization: Alter byte lengths and truncate trailing/leading bytes to discover block size (8 or 16 bytes) and cipher mode (ECB, CBC) from backend error responses. 5) Block alignment and forgery: Apply chosen-plaintext padding to align injected tokens with cipher blocks, trim static prefix blocks, and evaluate whether reconstructed tokens authenticate successfully.

metadata.title: Auditing for Symmetric Encryption Oracles and Cross-Context Key Reuse

text: Methodology for auditing multi-layer email parser discrepancies and differential interpretation: 1) Restriction profiling: Submit unauthorized email domains to identify regex boundaries and domain whitelists. 2) MIME Encoded-Word fuzzing: Inject RFC 2047 encapsulation schemes (=?charset?encoding?encoded-text?=) using standard charsets (utf-8, us-ascii, iso-8859-1) across both Q (Quoted-Printable) and B (Base64) formats into the local-part and domain segments. 3) Obsolete charset mutation: Probe uncommon, legacy, or multi-byte encodings (e.g., utf-7, euc-jp, shift_jis, iso-2022-jp) to discover validation filter bypasses. 4) Host delimiter injection: Inject encoded delimiter characters (&AEA- for '@', unicode nulls, space padding, or escaped quotes) to test whether downstream MTAs treat the encoded block as the true recipient address while upstream validators evaluate the static trailing string.

metadata.title: Auditing Email Normalization and Parser Discrepancies via Encoding Fuzzing

text: Testing Methodology: Misuse Case Modeling and Finite State Testing for Business Logic: 1) Workflow Deconstruction: Map the complete business process, identifying business limits, behavioral assumptions, and explicit transition rules ($S_0 \to S_1 \to ... \to S_n$). 2) Misuse Case Development: Formulate test cases violating conventional assumptions—skipping intermediate verification states, executing steps in reverse, repeating non-idempotent operations, or dropping transition tokens. 3) Parameter and State Tampering: Utilize intercepting proxies (e.g., OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite) to inspect and manipulate parameters in transit, testing whether modifying read-only values or altering sequential order alters the application logic flow. 4) Asynchronous and Resource Boundary Auditing: Evaluate concurrency, timeout limits on reserved resources, and ledger updates during cancellation or unexpected workflow interruptions.

metadata.title: Finite State Machine and Misuse Case Testing Methodology

text: Methodology for Auditing Business Logic Data Validation (WSTG-BUSL-01): 1) Handoff Surface Mapping: Enumerate all data entry points and trace parameter propagation across multi-tiered workflows, back-office connectors, third-party logistics APIs, and payment aggregators. 2) Interception & Semantic Mutation: Use intercepting proxies (e.g., OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite) to inject syntactically conforming but logically invalid payloads (e.g., validly formatted SSNs belonging to deceased individuals, non-existent warehouse routing IDs, or contradictory product configurations). 3) Boundary & Routing Divergence Testing: Alter fulfillment flags, delivery method enums, or inventory status variables to determine if downstream processors accept conflicting instructions without re-checking primary database state. 4) Concurrency & Cache Window Probing: Dispatch parallel requests across multiple sessions during scheduled batch update intervals to verify whether cached validation checks permit state transitions that exceed real-time resource limits.

metadata.title: Auditing Semantic Data Validation and Multi-Tier Integration Handoffs

text: Testing Methodology for Auditing Request Forgery and Parameter Guessing (WSTG-BUSL-02): 1) Hidden Field Discovery: Enumerate hidden HTML form elements, serialized JSON attributes, and query flags across multi-stage processes. 2) Flag Inversion Testing: Identify boolean or enumerated state parameters (e.g., is_submitted=1, paid=false, role=0) and invert them during downstream operations to observe application behavior. 3) Heuristic Parameter Fuzzing: Fuzz endpoints with common debug and administrative flags (e.g., debug=1, admin=true, test=1, trace=true, verbose=1) using tools like Burp Suite or OWASP ZAP. 4) Predictable Identifier Manipulation: Inspect sequential transaction numbers or identifiers and mutate them to access or modify records belonging to other tenants or previous workflow states.

metadata.title: Methodology for Auditing Request Forgery and State Manipulation

text: Methodology for Auditing Business Logic Integrity Checks (WSTG-BUSL-03): 1) UI vs. Payload Differential Mapping: Compare rendered DOM inputs (disabled, hidden, select controls) with outgoing HTTP parameters captured in an intercepting proxy. 2) Non-Editable Parameter Fuzzing: Manually append or mutate parameters designated as fixed/read-only on the frontend to determine if server controllers accept client overrides. 3) Relational Scoping and Enumeration: Identify dropdown menus and enumerated selectors; substitute values with adjacent, non-assigned, or privileged object IDs to evaluate server-side relational authorization. 4) Referential Consistency Testing: Submit edge-case attribute pairings that violate business logic rules (e.g., impossible entity statuses, mutually exclusive options) to evaluate relational constraint checks. 5) Audit Log Resiliency Testing: Probe logging endpoints with newline injection, format string tokens, or direct file manipulation attempts to assess log immutability.

metadata.title: Auditing Relational Integrity Checks and Hidden Field Constraints

text: Methodology for Auditing Process Timing and Transactional Lifecycles (WSTG-BUSL-04): 1) Statistical Timing Side-Channel Analysis: Transmit multi-round serialized requests across valid and invalid parameter sets (e.g., username lists, coupon tokens) and compute latency confidence intervals to identify information disclosure. 2) Resource Hold and Lockout Probing: Invoke reservation endpoints (POST /reserve, POST /cart/hold) and monitor secondary concurrent sessions at incremental delays (e.g., 5 min, 15 min, 60 min) to evaluate release mechanics and DOS impact. 3) Stalled Workflow Submission: In workflows featuring dynamic pricing or expiring terms, obtain a transaction token at $T_0$, pause submission via proxy intercept or script sleep, and submit at $T_{extended}$ to verify whether the backend rejects stale state or updates pricing.

metadata.title: Auditing Timing Side-Channels and Stalled Transaction Windows

text: Methodology for Auditing Function Execution Limits (WSTG-BUSL-05): 1) Identification: Catalog all high-value endpoints enforcing operational quotas (e.g., discount coupons, free trials, document exports, voting buttons). 2) Direct Replay Testing: Intercept the execution request using Burp Suite or OWASP ZAP; replay the exact payload immediately after initial consumption to verify single-use enforcement. 3) Workflow Navigation Perturbation: Execute the target action, navigate backward in the browser session, alter unrelated cart/profile attributes, and attempt to invoke the restricted function again. 4) Concurrency Fuzzing: Dispatch concurrent parallel requests for single-use actions using Turbo Intruder to identify race conditions in quota decrement routines.

metadata.title: Auditing Function Use Limits, Replay Controls, and Quota Bounds

text: Methodology for Auditing Workflow Circumvention and Sequence Bypasses (WSTG-BUSL-06): 1) Workflow Mapping: Deconstruct multi-stage operations into discrete states, documenting side-effects triggered at each transition ($S_0 \to S_1 \to ... \to S_n$). 2) Rollback & Abort Fuzzing: Progress through transactions to points where side-effects trigger, then issue cancellations, timeouts, or cart deductions to evaluate whether rollback mechanisms are atomic and complete. 3) Order Permutation Testing: Attempt forced browsing, out-of-order execution, and repetition of non-idempotent steps using Burp Proxy or OWASP ZAP. 4) Lifecycle Differential Auditing: Compare validation mechanisms between primary creation interfaces and secondary edit/append endpoints by injecting restricted or non-compliant values into update requests.

metadata.title: Auditing Workflow Sequence Enforcement and Rollback Integrity

text: Methodology for Auditing Application-Layer Active Defenses (WSTG-BUSL-07): 1) Anomaly Test Matrix Execution: Construct a synthetic battery of misuse actions across an active session, including parameter pollution (duplicate parameters), malformed data formats (truncated JSON/XML), rapid HTTP verb switching, and unauthorized entity ID references. 2) Behavioral Velocity Probing: Dispatch business operations (e.g., voucher redemptions, profile edits, checkout reviews) at rates exceeding human capability to evaluate behavioral velocity thresholds. 3) Countermeasure Profiling: Observe server responses across the testing sequence to determine whether defenses are purely localized (e.g., single-field rejection) or systemic (e.g., session-wide tarpitting, account suspension, challenge screens). 4) Out-of-Order Workflow Injection: Intentionally violate finite state machine paths to test if invalid state jumps generate security containment events or fail open.

metadata.title: Auditing Systemic Misuse Detection and Adaptive Response Mechanisms

text: Methodology for Auditing Unexpected File Type Handling (WSTG-BUSL-08): 1) Business File Specification Review: Catalog all expected file types and operational constraints for each upload endpoint. 2) Extension & Payload Library Generation: Assemble test payloads spanning server executable scripts (.php, .jsp, .asp, .cgi), scriptable formats (.html, .svg, .xml), and unexpected binaries (.exe, .sh). 3) Multi-Vector Bypassing: Test for superficial verification tiers by: bypassing client-side JavaScript validation with an intercepting proxy; preserving dangerous extensions while modifying the Content-Type header to permitted values; mutating filename extensions (e.g., double extensions .php.jpg, null byte injections .php%00.jpg, case alterations .PhP). 4) Archive Extraction Testing: Submit ZIP/TAR archives containing nested path traversal tokens (../../shell.php) to assess extraction directory containment. 5) Execution Verification: Attempt to retrieve and invoke the uploaded files directly via the browser or API client to determine execution contexts.

metadata.title: Auditing File Upload Boundaries, MIME Validation, and Storage Execution

text: Methodology for Auditing Malicious File Ingestion and Content Defenses (WSTG-BUSL-09): 1) Functional Inventory: Map all endpoints handling file uploads, identifying allowed MIME types, intended consumers, storage locations, and downstream decompression/rendering pipelines. 2) Antivirus & Antimalware Probing: Upload harmless standard test signatures (EICAR) across permitted extension wrappers to verify if active pipeline scanning is present. 3) Extension & MIME Evasion Fuzzing: Probe upload handlers using alternative execution extensions (.phtml, .php5, .shtml, .aspx, .cshtml), case variations, trailing dots/spaces/null-bytes, and mismatched Content-Type headers. 4) Archive Path Traversal & Zip Bomb Testing: Craft ZIP files embedding path traversal sequences (..\) and high-ratio sparse files to evaluate directory extraction boundaries and resource consumption ceilings. 5) Polyglot & Macro Injection: Test file uploads containing embedded payloads (e.g., PHP code inside valid image headers, JavaScript in PDFs, CSV macro formulas) to determine if files are re-encoded and sanitized prior to storage.
